security_audit.summary: The 76 static alerts reflect ordinary imports, exports, save discovery, binary constants, or documentation rather than the reported threats. Two semantic risks remain: partial writes after patch validation failures and symlink exposure through a predictable temporary filename. No evidence found of exfiltration, malware, or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: A plan can partially modify a save when some patches fail validation.
remediation.suggestion: Abort before backup or writing if any patch fails; reject overlapping patches and return a nonzero status for incomplete plans.

remediation.issue: The predictable temporary filename can follow an existing symbolic link and overwrite another writable file.
remediation.suggestion: Create an exclusive, randomly named temporary file in the target directory; write through its descriptor before replacing the target.

semantic_findings.title: Failed patches do not prevent a partial save write
semantic_findings.description: Validation failures skip individual patches, but application continues if any patch succeeds. The resulting partial save is written and reported with a zero status.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code aborts only when no patches apply, not when any patch fails. Related game-state changes can therefore become inconsistent despite backups.

semantic_findings.title: Predictable temporary path can overwrite a symlink destination
semantic_findings.description: Atomic writes use a fixed sibling filename and write_bytes follows existing symlinks. An attacker controlling that directory could redirect writes to another writable file.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The temporary path is deterministic and opened without exclusive creation or symlink rejection. Exploitation requires directory access and a writable destination.

content.user_title: Prepare Gallery Unlock Patches for Offline Game Saves
content.value_statement: Gallery unlock flags can be difficult to locate in local game saves. This skill combines save discovery, RGSS inspection, and byte comparisons to prepare reviewable patches.
actual_capabilities: Search common local save directories and rank candidates by names, extensions, location, and modification time.
Identify several game engines from installation files and directory markers.
Inspect RGSS Marshal save streams and generate plans for selected switches or integer variable assignments.
Compare two save snapshots and export changed byte ranges with file hashes.
Infer candidate flag layouts from single-byte changes, with optional explicit start, stride, and slot count.
Preview and apply patch plans, create default backups, verify expected bytes, and restore recorded backups.
limitations: Dedicated save parsing is provided for RGSS; other engines may require manual format analysis or controlled comparisons.
Encrypted, compressed, signed, or reordered saves need separate analysis; the skill does not provide universal decoding.
Gallery-related switch meanings are game-specific; unrelated switches can alter story progress or failure conditions.
Partial patch failures can still write changes, and temporary writes need hardening against existing symlinks.

best_practices: Close the game, confirm ownership and offline operation, and keep an independent untouched backup.
Use absolute paths and confirmed gallery flags; prefer explicit layout parameters over automatic extrapolation.
Review the entire dry-run report, stop on any failure, and validate successful changes inside the game.
anti_patterns: Enable every switch without confirming whether it controls gallery access, story progression, or failure states.
Apply unreviewed plans, bypass backups, or continue after validation failures.
Use the workflow for multiplayer games, online verification bypasses, DRM circumvention, or distribution of copyrighted resources.

faq.question: Which games have dedicated save support?
faq.answer: The bundled adapter targets RPG Maker XP, VX, and VX Ace RGSS saves. Other engines rely on documentation and generic comparison.

faq.question: Does it automatically identify every gallery flag?
faq.answer: No. It locates data and proposes patches, but game-specific gallery meanings require confirmation.

faq.question: Can it decode encrypted or signed saves?
faq.answer: No universal decoder is included. Unsupported compression, encryption, and signatures can prevent reliable comparison or patching.

faq.question: Does it support online or multiplayer games?
faq.answer: No. The documented scope excludes multiplayer, leaderboards, online validation, and anti-cheat systems.

faq.question: How do backups and rollback work?
faq.answer: Application creates a timestamped backup by default and records its path and hash. Rollback checks the recorded hash when present before restoring.

faq.question: What should I do when a dry-run reports failures?
faq.answer: Stop and regenerate or correct the plan. The current implementation can apply successful patches even when other patches fail.
